endpoints.summary: Lists appointments for the caller. Three role branches decided in-handler: PHYSICIAN (by JWT userType) -> own appointments by physicianProfile.id; non-physician WITH a resolvable staff clinic (X-Clinic-Id header or ?clinicId) -> all appointments of that clinic; everyone else -> own bookings by patientUserId. Optional status/date/clinicId filters, ordered by appointmentDate asc, hard-capped at 200 rows. Physician and clinic-staff branches get a batch patientUser enrichment appended to each row.
endpoints.auth: Global: helmet, compression, cors, body sanitizer, express-rate-limit 100 req/min per IP on /api. Router: authCheck (L18, JWT Bearer -> req.user = {id,email,role,userType,displayName,organizationId,iat,exp}). Route: cacheMiddleware(15). In-handler gate: req.user.userType === 'PHYSICIAN' string compare, else prisma.clinicStaff.findFirst({userId, clinicId: req.headers['x-clinic-id'] || query.clinicId, isActive:true}); NO aiUsageCheck, NO auditLog.
requestQuery: status?: string - passed straight through to prisma as AppointmentStatus enum, NOT validated ('PENDING'|'CONFIRMED'|'COMPLETED'|'CANCELLED'|'NO_SHOW')
date?: string - any Date-parseable string; used as `new Date(date)` then setHours(0,0,0,0) / setHours(23,59,59,999) in SERVER LOCAL time
clinicId?: string - doubles as the staff-clinic resolver AND as an extra where filter applied after the branch logic
endpoints.responseShape:
// Branch A - userType==='PHYSICIAN' OR staff clinic resolved (where.clinicId set): JSON array (possibly empty), each element:
[
  {
    "id": "uuid",
    "clinicId": "uuid",
    "physicianId": "uuid",
    "patientUserId": "uuid",
    "subprofileId": "uuid | null",
    "clinicPatientId": "uuid | null",
    "status": "PENDING | CONFIRMED | COMPLETED | CANCELLED | NO_SHOW",
    "appointmentDate": "2026-03-10T00:00:00.000Z",   // ISO-8601 UTC string w/ ms (Date.toJSON)
    "startTime": "09:00",                             // plain string, NOT a time type
    "endTime": "09:30",                               // plain string
    "reason": "string | null",
    "notes": "string | null",                         // may contain 'WALK_IN' and/or '\nCHECKIN:{json}' markers
    "appointmentType": "IN_PERSON | VIDEO | PHONE | WALK_IN",
    "confirmedAt": "ISO string | null",
    "completedAt": "ISO string | null",
    "cancelledAt": "ISO string | null",
    "cancelReason": "string | null",
    "recurringRule": "string | null",                 // 'WEEKLY'|'BIWEEKLY'|'MONTHLY'|null, free-text column
    "recurringGroupId": "uuid | null",
    "createdAt": "ISO string",
    "updatedAt": "ISO string",
    "deletedAt": "ISO string | null",                 // soft-delete column IS emitted and NOT filtered
    "clinic": { "id": "uuid", "name": "string", "address": "string | null", "phone": "string | null" },
    "physician": { "specialty": "string", "user": { "displayName": "string" } },
    "subprofile": { "name": "string", "relation": "SELF|SPOUSE|CHILD|PARENT|SIBLING|OTHER" } | null,
    "patientUser": { "id": "uuid", "displayName": "string", "phone": "string | null" } | null
  }
]

// Branch B - non-physician, no staff clinic resolved and no ?clinicId: IDENTICAL element shape
// EXCEPT the "patientUser" key is ABSENT ENTIRELY (not null). clinic/physician/subprofile still present.

// Branch C - userType==='PHYSICIAN' but no PhysicianProfile row: literally []

// Key order (matters for byte-identical JSON): all Appointment scalars in prisma schema order,
// then clinic, physician, subprofile (include declaration order), then patientUser appended last by the spread.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing or not 'Bearer '-prefixed
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws (bad signature, expired)
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter (100/min/IP)

500 {"error":"Failed to list appointments"} on any thrown error - INCLUDING an invalid ?status value (prisma enum validation) and an unparseable ?date (Invalid Date reaches prisma). There is NO 400 validation on this route.
crossModelReads: Clinic (via include: id, name, address, phone)
User (findMany by id IN - id, displayName, phone)
sideEffects: Writes the successful response object into the in-process cache under key `route:{userId}:{req.originalUrl}` for 15s
Request log line via logger.info in the global middleware
quirks: RESPONSE-SHAPE FORK: `patientUser` is present (object-or-null) for physicians and clinic-staff, and COMPLETELY ABSENT for a plain patient. A .NET port that always emits patientUser:null changes the payload for patient callers.

`patientUser` also appears for a PATIENT caller who merely passes ?clinicId=... - the enrichment condition is `userType==='PHYSICIAN' || where.clinicId`, and where.clinicId gets set by the unconditional `if (clinicId) where.clinicId = clinicId` at the end, regardless of staff membership. So a patient with ?clinicId gets their own name/phone echoed back.
Missing PhysicianProfile for a PHYSICIAN returns 200 [] - not 404, not 403.
Silent `take: 200` cap with no total/hasMore/pagination signal. The 201st appointment simply does not exist to the client.

The ?date day-boundary is computed as `new Date(date)` (UTC-midnight for a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD') then `.setHours(0,0,0,0)` in SERVER LOCAL time. On a server west of UTC this shifts the window to the PREVIOUS calendar day. Note this differs from GET /available which uses `new Date(date+'T00:00:00')` (local midnight directly) - the two endpoints disagree about what 'that day' means.
Staff clinic id is read from the lowercased header `x-clinic-id` FIRST, falling back to ?clinicId.
A non-physician who sends a clinic id but is NOT active staff silently falls back to `where.patientUserId = userId` - a 200 with their own (usually empty) list, never a 403.

CACHE KEY IGNORES THE HEADER: cacheMiddleware keys on `route:{userId}:{originalUrl}` only. A staff member switching clinics via X-Clinic-Id with an identical URL gets the OTHER clinic's cached list for up to 15s. Nothing in this router calls cache.invalidate, so POST / (booking) or PUT /:id/confirm also do not bust the 15s cache.
The cache is a per-process in-memory Map, so under PM2 cluster mode different workers return different generations of the same list.
`deletedAt` is returned and soft-deleted rows are NOT filtered out anywhere in this handler (no prisma soft-delete middleware exists - server/src/lib/prisma.js is a bare PrismaClient).
userType comes from the JWT payload, not from a live DB read - a stale token role decides the branch.
`physician.specialty` is exposed but `physician.id`/`userId` are not; the client cannot correlate the physician object back to an id from this endpoint.
Ordering is `appointmentDate: 'asc'` only - appointments on the same date come back in unspecified order (startTime is NOT a tiebreaker here, unlike /today and /queue).
startTime/endTime are strings ('09:00'); any sorting or comparison must be lexicographic, and a non-zero-padded value like '9:00' would sort after '10:00'.

endpoints.summary: Physician-only today's schedule. Resolves PhysicianProfile from req.user.id, fetches PENDING+CONFIRMED appointments whose appointmentDate falls in the server-local calendar day, ordered by the startTime STRING, then appends a batch-loaded patientUser {id,displayName} to each row. Any caller without a PhysicianProfile gets [].
endpoints.auth: Global: helmet/compression/cors/sanitizer + 100 req/min/IP on /api. Router: authCheck (L18). Route: cacheMiddleware(15). In-handler gate: existence of prisma.physicianProfile for req.user.id - NOT a userType check, and NO explicit 403. NO aiUsageCheck, NO auditLog.
endpoints.responseShape:
// JSON array (possibly empty), each element:
[
  {
    "id": "uuid",
    "clinicId": "uuid",
    "physicianId": "uuid",
    "patientUserId": "uuid",
    "subprofileId": "uuid | null",
    "clinicPatientId": "uuid | null",
    "status": "PENDING | CONFIRMED",                  // only these two can appear (where-filtered)
    "appointmentDate": "2026-09-03T00:00:00.000Z",     // ISO-8601 UTC string w/ ms
    "startTime": "09:00",
    "endTime": "09:30",
    "reason": "string | null",
    "notes": "string | null",
    "appointmentType": "IN_PERSON | VIDEO | PHONE | WALK_IN",
    "confirmedAt": "ISO string | null",
    "completedAt": "ISO string | null",
    "cancelledAt": "ISO string | null",
    "cancelReason": "string | null",
    "recurringRule": "string | null",
    "recurringGroupId": "uuid | null",
    "createdAt": "ISO string",
    "updatedAt": "ISO string",
    "deletedAt": "ISO string | null",
    "clinic": { "name": "string" },                    // NAME ONLY - no id, no address, no phone
    "subprofile": { "name": "string", "relation": "SELF|SPOUSE|CHILD|PARENT|SIBLING|OTHER" } | null,
    "patientUser": { "id": "uuid", "displayName": "string" } | null   // NO phone here
  }
]

// Key order: Appointment scalars in schema order, then clinic, then subprofile, then patientUser (spread, last).
// There is NO "physician" key on this endpoint.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing/malformed
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global limiter
500 {"error":"Failed to get today schedule"} on any thrown error
NOTE: no 403 and no 404 exist on this route - a patient or receptionist gets 200 []
crossModelReads: User (findMany by id IN - id, displayName)
externalDeps: cacheMiddleware / lib/cache (15s TTL, key includes no query so it is just `route:{userId}:/api/appointments/today`)
quirks: A non-physician (patient, receptionist) gets 200 [] rather than 403. The endpoint is 'physician-only' by silent fallthrough.
clinic here is `{ name }` ONLY - deliberately narrower than GET / which returns {id,name,address,phone}. Do not reuse one DTO for both.
patientUser here is `{ id, displayName }` with NO phone - GET / includes phone, GET /queue includes phone but NOT id. Three different patient shapes across the three list endpoints.
No `physician` key at all on this endpoint.
`orderBy: { startTime: 'asc' }` sorts the STRING column, so a non-zero-padded '9:00' sorts after '10:00'. Must be replicated as an ordinal string sort, not a parsed-time sort.

Day window is built from server local time: `new Date(y, m, d)` .. `new Date(y, m, d, 23,59,59,999)`. The comparison against a UTC-stored DateTime means 'today' is the server's timezone day, not the physician's or the client's.
Only PENDING and CONFIRMED are returned - COMPLETED, CANCELLED and NO_SHOW appointments vanish from today's list once acted on. (Contrast GET /queue, which keeps COMPLETED and NO_SHOW.)
Soft-deleted rows (deletedAt != null) are still returned, and deletedAt is emitted.
patientUser is `null` when the patient User row is missing (deleted user) - the array element still appears.
The endOfDay ms component is 999, so an appointmentDate at exactly 23:59:59.9995 would be excluded; port must use lte with .999.
Nothing invalidates the 15s cache, so a check-in or confirm made in the same window is invisible to /today for up to 15s.

endpoints.summary: Today's clinic-wide patient queue for staff/assistants. Requires ?clinicId. Access = physician who OWNS that clinic, or active ClinicStaff there. Returns today's PENDING/CONFIRMED/COMPLETED/NO_SHOW appointments for the clinic, ordered by startTime string, each enriched with patientUser, check-in state parsed out of the free-text notes column, and today's Visit status overlaid. Wrapped in { queue, summary }.
endpoints.auth: Global: helmet/compression/cors/sanitizer + 100 req/min/IP. Router: authCheck (L18). NO cacheMiddleware on this route. In-handler gate: prisma.physicianProfile.findUnique({where:{userId}, include:{clinics:{where:{id:clinicId}, take:1}}}) -> isPhysician = physician && physician.clinics.length > 0; else prisma.clinicStaff.findFirst({userId, clinicId, isActive:true}); 403 if neither. NO aiUsageCheck, NO auditLog.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "queue": [
    {
      // --- Appointment scalars, prisma schema order ---
      "id": "uuid",
      "clinicId": "uuid",
      "physicianId": "uuid",
      "patientUserId": "uuid",
      "subprofileId": "uuid | null",
      "clinicPatientId": "uuid | null",
      "status": "PENDING | CONFIRMED | COMPLETED | NO_SHOW",   // CANCELLED never appears
      "appointmentDate": "2026-09-03T00:00:00.000Z",
      "startTime": "09:00",
      "endTime": "09:30",
      "reason": "string | null",
      "notes": "string | null",                  // raw, still containing 'WALK_IN' / 'CHECKIN:{...}'
      "appointmentType": "IN_PERSON | VIDEO | PHONE | WALK_IN",
      "confirmedAt": "ISO string | null",
      "completedAt": "ISO string | null",
      "cancelledAt": "ISO string | null",
      "cancelReason": "string | null",
      "recurringRule": "string | null",
      "recurringGroupId": "uuid | null",
      "createdAt": "ISO string",
      "updatedAt": "ISO string",
      "deletedAt": "ISO string | null",

      // --- includes, in declaration order ---
      "subprofile": { "name": "string", "relation": "SELF|SPOUSE|CHILD|PARENT|SIBLING|OTHER" } | null,
      "physician": {                              // full include -> EVERY PhysicianProfile scalar
        "id": "uuid",
        "userId": "uuid",
        "licenseNumber": "string",
        "specialty": "string",
        "qualifications": "string | null",
        "bio": "string | null",
        "scratchpadNotes": "string | null",       // private physician scratchpad LEAKS to staff here
        "yearsOfExperience": 0,                    // int | null
        "verified": false,
        "verifiedAt": "ISO string | null",
        "createdAt": "ISO string",
        "updatedAt": "ISO string",
        "user": { "displayName": "string" }
      },

      // --- appended by the first map (spread order) ---
      "patientUser": { "displayName": "string", "phone": "string | null" } | null,  // NO id
      "checkedIn": false,                          // boolean, derived from notes
      "checkedInAt": "2026-09-03T08:41:12.113Z",   // STRING copied verbatim out of the notes JSON, or null
      "room": "string | null",                     // whatever was stored in the notes JSON (may be any JSON type)

      // --- appended by the visit-overlay map ---
      "visitStatus": "IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED | CANCELLED | ARCHIVED | null",
      "visitFollowUp": "ISO string | null",        // <- Visit.followUpDate, RENAMED
      "visitFollowUpNotes": "string | null",       // <- Visit.followUpNotes, RENAMED
      "visitCompletedAt": "ISO string | null"      // <- Visit.completedAt, RENAMED
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total": 0,
    "arrived": 0,
    "pending": 0,
    "completed": 0,
    "noShow": 0
  }
}

// "queue" is [] (never null) when the clinic has no appointments today; "summary" is then all zeros.
errorCases: 400 {"error":"clinicId required"} when ?clinicId is missing or falsy
403 {"error":"Not staff at this clinic"} when the caller is neither the owning physician of that clinic nor an active ClinicStaff row for it
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global limiter
500 {"error":"Failed to load queue"} on any thrown error
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId, include filtered clinics relation; then FULL scalar set exposed via the appointment include)
Clinic (only as the filtered `clinics` relation used for the ownership check)
Visit (findMany - id, patientUserId, status, followUpDate, followUpNotes, completedAt)
quirks: RESPONSE IS AN ENVELOPE `{queue, summary}` - unlike GET / and GET /today which return bare arrays.
There is NO `clinic` key on queue rows even though clinicId is required - the client already knows the clinic. Do not add one.

`physician` is a FULL prisma `include` (no select), so every PhysicianProfile scalar ships to every receptionist, including `bio` and `scratchpadNotes` (the physician's private notes) and `licenseNumber`. A faithful port MUST emit all of these or the JSON differs; flag it separately as a data-exposure issue rather than silently trimming.
`patientUser` here is `{displayName, phone}` with NO `id` - different from GET / ({id,displayName,phone}) and GET /today ({id,displayName}).

RESPONSE KEY RENAMES: visitFollowUp <- Visit.followUpDate, visitFollowUpNotes <- Visit.followUpNotes, visitCompletedAt <- Visit.completedAt. The Visit's own `id` IS selected from the DB but is NEVER emitted - it is dropped by the merge.

checkedIn/checkedInAt/room are reverse-engineered from the free-text `notes` column: trigger is `notes.includes('CHECKIN:')`, payload is `notes.split('CHECKIN:').pop()` (LAST occurrence wins) parsed as JSON. On JSON.parse failure the catch sets checkedIn = true but LEAVES checkedInAt = null and room = null - i.e. 'checked in at unknown time'. Port must copy this partial-success path exactly.

checkedInAt is a STRING carried straight out of the notes JSON (written as `new Date().toISOString()` by PUT /:id/check-in), NOT a re-serialized Date. It is not normalized or validated, and its format therefore does not necessarily match the Date-derived ISO fields next to it.
`room` is whatever JSON value was stored (normally a string or null, but a numeric room from the client stays numeric). Do not coerce it to string.

Visit overlay is keyed only by patientUserId with NO orderBy on the visit query, so when one patient has MULTIPLE visits today the LAST row returned by the DB wins - non-deterministic. Also the overlay is not scoped to the appointment, so a walk-in visit attaches to an unrelated appointment row of the same patient.
Visit overlay does not filter Visit.deletedAt or Visit.physicianId - any visit at that clinic today for that patient matches, including a soft-deleted one and one by a different physician.

SUMMARY BUCKETS OVERLAP AND DO NOT SUM TO total: `pending` = !checkedIn && status !== 'COMPLETED', so a NO_SHOW that was never checked in is counted in BOTH `pending` and `noShow`; and a checked-in NO_SHOW counts in both `arrived` and `noShow`. Reproduce the predicates literally, do not 'fix' the arithmetic.
`arrived` counts the notes-derived checkedIn flag, not appointment status - a CONFIRMED appointment with no CHECKIN marker is not 'arrived'.
CANCELLED is excluded from the status filter, so cancelled appointments silently disappear from the queue and from every summary count.

N+1 by design: one `prisma.user.findUnique` per appointment inside Promise.all. Result order is preserved by map, so output order still follows the startTime sort - a batched .NET implementation must preserve that same order.

Physician ownership check uses the filtered `clinics` relation (`clinics.length > 0`), so a physician querying a clinic they do not own falls through to the STAFF check and can still pass if they happen to be staff there.
Day window uses server-local `new Date(y,m,d)` .. `(y,m,d,23,59,59,999)` for BOTH appointments and visits.
`orderBy: { startTime: 'asc' }` is a string sort (same padding caveat as /today).
Not cached - fresh on every call, unlike / and /today.

There is no GET /:id route anywhere in this router, so /queue and /ai-optimize (both declared AFTER `router.delete('/:id')`) are NOT shadowed. A .NET port that adds a `GET /{id}` route WILL shadow /queue, /today, /available and /ai-optimize unless the literal routes are registered first.

endpoints.summary: Returns a physician's recurring TimeSlot template for the weekday of a given date, each slot flagged isBooked. Requires physicianUserId + date; clinicId optional. If the clinic has allowPatientBooking=false, only the physician themselves or active clinic staff may see slots - anyone else gets []. Slots are de-duplicated by startTime and every slot is returned (booked ones are marked, not removed).
endpoints.auth: Global: helmet/compression/cors/sanitizer + 100 req/min/IP. Router: authCheck (L18) - any authenticated user may probe any physician. Route: NO cacheMiddleware. In-handler gate (only when ?clinicId is supplied AND clinic.allowPatientBooking === false): isOwner = req.user?.id === query.physicianUserId, else prisma.clinicStaff.findFirst({clinicId, userId: req.user.id, isActive:true}); failure returns 200 [] not 403. NO aiUsageCheck, NO auditLog.
requestQuery: physicianUserId: string (REQUIRED - this is the USER id, not the PhysicianProfile id)
date: string 'YYYY-MM-DD' (REQUIRED - concatenated as `date+'T12:00:00'` for weekday and `date+'T00:00:00'` / `date+'T23:59:59.999'` for the booked-window, all LOCAL time)
clinicId?: string - when absent, slots from ALL of the physician's clinics are merged
errorCases: 400 {"error":"physicianUserId and date are required"} when either is missing/falsy
200 [] when no PhysicianProfile exists for physicianUserId (NOT 404)
200 [] when clinic.allowPatientBooking === false and the caller is neither the physician nor active staff (NOT 403)
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global limiter
500 {"error":"Failed to check availability"} on any thrown error - including a malformed ?date (Invalid Date -> getDay() NaN -> prisma validation error). No 400 for bad date format.
crossModelReads: Clinic (findUnique - allowPatientBooking, physicianId; and via include - name)
quirks: THREE DIFFERENT 'not allowed' outcomes all return 200 [] - missing physician profile, booking-disabled clinic with an unauthorized caller. Never 403/404. A port that returns 403 breaks the client, which just renders 'no slots'.

The booking gate is only evaluated when ?clinicId is supplied. Omit clinicId and the allowPatientBooking=false protection is bypassed entirely - slots from booking-disabled clinics are returned to any authenticated user.
The gate's owner check compares `req.user.id === physicianUserId` (the query string), NOT the resolved PhysicianProfile - a string compare against untrusted input.
`clinic.physicianId` is selected in the gate query but never used.

Weekday is derived from `new Date(date + 'T12:00:00')` - LOCAL NOON, deliberately, to dodge DST/midnight rollover. A port that parses the date as UTC midnight will pick the wrong dayOfWeek for negative-UTC-offset servers.

The booked-appointments window uses `new Date(date+'T00:00:00')` .. `new Date(date+'T23:59:59.999')` (local), which is a DIFFERENT construction from GET /'s `new Date(date)` + setHours. The two endpoints can disagree on which day a boundary appointment belongs to.

Booked-detection is by startTime STRING EQUALITY only (`Set` of appointment.startTime). endTime is selected from the DB and never used, so overlapping-but-not-identical bookings do NOT mark a slot booked, and a slot whose startTime string differs only in padding ('9:00' vs '09:00') reads as free.
The booked query is scoped by physicianId and date ONLY - NOT by clinicId. An appointment the physician has at clinic B at 09:00 marks the 09:00 slot at clinic A as booked.
Booked statuses are PENDING and CONFIRMED only - COMPLETED, CANCELLED and NO_SHOW appointments free the slot back up.

De-duplication by startTime keeps the FIRST slot seen in `orderBy: {startTime:'asc'}` order and discards the rest. With no ?clinicId this collapses same-time slots ACROSS DIFFERENT CLINICS, so only one clinic's slot survives and the surviving row's clinicId/clinic.name is effectively arbitrary among ties.
Booked slots are RETURNED with isBooked:true, not filtered out - the client is responsible for disabling them.
`isActive: true` is in the where clause yet the field is still emitted on every row (always true).
Slots are the recurring weekly TEMPLATE - there is no per-date slot storage, no holiday/blackout handling, and past dates return the same list as future dates.
`orderBy: { startTime: 'asc' }` is a string sort, and the de-dup depends on that order, so the sort must be replicated as an ordinal string sort or the surviving duplicate changes.
Empty array vs null: always an array, never null.
Not cached, unlike / and /today.

endpoints.summary: Physician-only scheduling analytics. Stage 1 aggregates 90 days of the physician's appointments (plus completed visit durations and active time slots) into a large computed `stats` object entirely in JS. Stage 2 sends that stats JSON to the AI gateway asking for 3-5 scheduling insights, parses/sanitizes the JSON array it gets back, and returns { stats, insights, aiProvider }. Any AI failure degrades to insights:[] with stats intact.
endpoints.auth: Global: helmet/compression/cors/sanitizer + 100 req/min/IP. Router: authCheck (L18). NO cacheMiddleware. In-handler gate: prisma.physicianProfile.findUnique({where:{userId}}) -> 403 if absent. NO aiUsageCheck (no quota/plan check at all on this AI call), NO auditLog middleware - but aiGateway.chat writes its own AiAuditLog row.
errorCases: 403 {"error":"Only physicians can access scheduling insights"} when no PhysicianProfile exists for req.user.id
200 {"stats":null,"insights":[],"message":"Not enough appointment data for analysis. Need at least 5 appointments in the last 90 days."} when fewer than 5 appointments matched
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global limiter
500 {"error":"Failed to generate scheduling insights"} only if Stage 1 (the DB/aggregation part) throws - AI failures are swallowed and never produce a 5xx
dbWrites: AiAuditLog - one row per call, written inside aiGateway.logAudit (NOT in a transaction, errors swallowed). Fields: agent='scheduler', provider, model, userId, inputHash(sha256 of system+user), tokensUsed, costUsd, latencyMs, success, errorMsg, cached, metadata. Written on cache hit (tokensUsed 0, cached true), on success, and on total provider failure (provider='none', model=null, success=false).
crossModelReads: Visit (findMany - visitDate, completedAt; status COMPLETED, completedAt not null, visitDate gte 90d)
externalDeps: services/aiGateway - lazily `require`d INSIDE the try block; ai.chat({system,user,temperature:0.2,maxTokens:1200,useCache:true,metadata:{agent:'scheduler',userId}})
OpenAI / Gemini / MicroMind HTTP APIs via the aiGateway provider chain
aiGateway's own in-process response cache (keyed by sha256 of system+user)
sideEffects: One outbound LLM call (unless the aiGateway prompt cache hits)
Token spend / cost - with NO quota or plan enforcement on this route
quirks: TWO DIFFERENT RESPONSE SHAPES: the <5-appointments branch has `message` and NO `aiProvider`; the normal branch has `aiProvider` and NO `message`. A port must omit the keys, not send them as null.

All rates are FRACTIONS 0..1 rounded to 3 decimals via `parseFloat(x.toFixed(3))`, not percentages. parseFloat drops trailing zeros, so 0.100 serializes as 0.1 and an exact 0 serializes as 0 (integer). .NET decimal/double formatting must match: round-half-away-from-zero at 3 dp then emit the shortest form.
`avgDailyPatients` uses toFixed(1) then parseFloat, so 3.0 serializes as 3 (no decimal point).
`slotUtilization` is computed with toFixed(3) and THEN wrapped in Math.min(x, 1) inside the stats literal - the cap is applied after rounding.
The 90-day window is `now - 90 days` KEEPING THE CURRENT TIME OF DAY (`setDate(getDate()-90)`), not a midnight boundary - so results shift within the day.

The window has NO UPPER BOUND (`appointmentDate: { gte: ninetyDaysAgo }`), so FUTURE appointments are included in every metric. 'Last 90 days' in the prompt text and message is a lie; noShowRate is diluted by unheld future bookings.
The <5 threshold counts ALL statuses including CANCELLED and future ones.
Soft-deleted appointments (deletedAt != null) and soft-deleted visits are NOT excluded.

`totalCapacity = activeSlots.length * Math.ceil(90/7)` = slots x 13. This treats the CURRENT slot template as if it had been in effect for all 13 weeks, and counts a weekly template row once per week - it is a rough proxy, not a real capacity figure. Copy the arithmetic literally, including the hard-coded ceil(90/7)=13.
`avgVisitDurationMin` is derived as (completedAt - visitDate)/60000 with outliers filtered to `> 0 && < 300` minutes; null when the list ends up empty. Math.round, so integer minutes.

`peakHour` is the raw hour KEY from startTime.split(':')[0] with ':00' appended - so a badly padded startTime '9:00' yields peakHour "9:00", not "09:00". Default when byHour is empty is '09' -> "09:00" (unreachable in practice given the >=5 guard).

`hourDistribution` is sorted with `a.hour.localeCompare(b.hour)` on the string - locale-sensitive string ordering, and mixed padding ('9:00' vs '09:00') sorts wrongly. Port with an ordinal string comparison to stay identical for padded data.

`dayStats` derives from `Object.entries(byDay)` where the keys are numeric strings - V8 enumerates integer-like keys ASCENDING, then Array.sort (stable) reorders by total DESC. Ties therefore keep ascending dayIndex order. A .NET Dictionary has no such guarantee: build the intermediate ordered by dayIndex ascending, then stable-sort by total descending.
`busiestDay` = dayStats[0]?.day || 'N/A' - the literal string "N/A" is a possible value.
Day names are hard-coded English, Sunday-first, and `dayIndex` is JS getDay() (0=Sunday). No localization even though the client is bilingual.
`analyzedDays` counts distinct `new Date(appointmentDate).toDateString()` values - SERVER-LOCAL day bucketing via a JS-specific format string.
`typeBreakdown` is a bare object map, not an array, and only contains types that actually occur (never zero-filled). Null appointmentType is bucketed as 'IN_PERSON'.

Key-name traps: `noShows` (plural) vs `noShowRate`; `cancelled` (two L's) vs `cancelRate` (one L, no -led); `avgVisitDurationMin` (Min suffix) vs `avgSlotDuration` (no suffix); `totalActiveSlotsPerWeek`; `analyzedDays`.

`aiProvider = result.provider` is assigned BEFORE the JSON parse, so a successful LLM call whose output fails to parse returns aiProvider set (e.g. "openai") together with insights:[]. Only a thrown ai.chat gives aiProvider:null.
AI text is de-fenced with `.replace(/```json\n?/g,'').replace(/```\n?/g,'').trim()` before JSON.parse; a non-array parse result is coerced to []; items missing type/title/description are dropped.
The sanitizer caps title at 120 and description at 500 chars and slices to 6 items, even though the system prompt asks for max 80 chars and 3-5 insights. The CODE limits are the contract.
insights ordering is whatever the LLM returned (post-filter) - the 'ordered by impact' instruction is not enforced in code.

insights is inherently NON-DETERMINISTIC across calls, but aiGateway's useCache:true means the same stats JSON returns the same cached text (and still writes an AiAuditLog row with tokensUsed 0, cached true).
The `id`, `endTime`, `clinicId`, `cancelledAt` and `cancelReason` fields are selected from appointments but never used in any metric - only status, appointmentDate, startTime and appointmentType are.
activeSlots is queried with no clinic scoping, so a physician with several clinics has their capacity/duration averages pooled across all of them.
No cacheMiddleware on this route, so every page load costs a DB aggregation and potentially an LLM call.
Declared after `router.delete('/:id')` but that is a DELETE handler, so no GET shadowing occurs in Node. Preserve literal-route-before-parameterized-route registration in .NET.
